manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the phone on the box and place it on the phone stand to the right.

Task description: Move the phone with a black screen and light-colored frame from the white box on the left to the white phone stand with a tilted backrest on its right, where the stand can support it securely.

Success criteria: The phone is placed securely on the stand to the right and remains in place after the gripper opens, without slipping or tipping.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping the middle sections of the phone's long edges, closing the fingers toward each other across its width. Leave the lower edge clear so the gripper does not interfere with seating it on the stand ledge.
- Open only slightly wider than the phone, leaving clearance for the pen and mouse on the box. Before closing, use both views to confirm the pads physically surround both frame edges, avoiding mere image overlap, screen pressure, or contact with the box surface.
- When adjusting the phone tilt, choose a position with clearance from clutter on the box and the phone stand, avoiding contact between the phone corners or gripper and nearby objects.
- Align the phone's lower edge with the stand's bottom support lip and gently rest its back against the inclined backplate. Leave finger-withdrawal space, avoiding landing outside the lip or pushing the stand over downward.
- Gradually release after confirming that the support edge is holding the phone. Watch whether the phone slides or the stand wobbles, then withdraw the fingers to avoid releasing before the phone is supported.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start one real-robot episode with the specified parameters, act on the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode when finished or unable to continue.

Only the right arm is available. The phone is on the box and the stand on the right is empty. I am adjusting gripper orientation and lateral position at height, then will reduce step size near the phone and confirm the grasp before lifting.

A pose adjustment reached the controller's joint limit and returned a recoverable rejection. Using the actual stopping position, I returned to a reachable pose. Next I will keep a shallower tilt and adjust the grasp position in small steps.

The gripper is nearly aligned with the phone's long edges, and the phone remains on the box. I am approaching in steps no larger than 1 cm, continuing to check the pads, phone frame, and nearby pen positions.

The phone has not been lifted. Both side frames are within the gripper opening, but I still need to confirm the pads have descended to frame height. I will continue with millimeter-scale adjustments, avoiding pressure on the screen or box surface.

After a small test lift, the phone did not leave the box surface with the gripper, so there is not yet a secure grasp. I reopened the gripper and will further adjust the height based on the current view.

The measured gripper opening stopped at about 75 mm, and the phone lifted off the box surface with a small upward movement. Next I will increase clearance from the box, adjust the phone’s tilt, and move it toward the stand on the right.

The phone slipped back onto the box while being lifted and tilted; the grasp did not hold. The stand remains empty. Within this episode, I will realign with the phone and try a more vertical side grip with deeper contact.
I have realigned with the phone and am moving the pads to a deeper contact point on its side edge. I will still test-lift first and transport it to the stand only after confirming a stable grasp.

This time the phone continued to rise with the gripper, with a clear gap between it and the box surface and no further slip. I am lifting higher and moving it to the right while adjusting the placement tilt.

The phone is held steadily and is above the stand's upper left. I am aligning it with the stand's backplate, then I will lower it in small steps so the bottom edge settles onto the ledge, gradually release, and check stability.

During lowering, the phone contacted the top edge of the stand and changed its tilt. I lifted to break contact. Next I will move slightly forward of the stand and realign with the bottom support ledge.

The phone slipped during retreat and landed on the table left of the stand rather than resting securely on it. I will confirm the stationary state and end this episode; available observations and remaining turns cannot support a reliable regrasp and placement.
